local_take: Northside is close to Downtown at a fraction of Heights prices. Block by block differences are big here, so drive it often.
best_for: Buyers and investors looking for value close to Downtown

name: Northwest Houston
summary: A broad area along Highway 290 and Beltway 8 with established subdivisions and easy commutes.
typical_homes: 1970s to 2000s single family homes and townhomes
local_take: Northwest Houston is a practical choice with lots of options. Compare MUD taxes and commute times between subdivisions.
best_for: Buyers who want value and highway access
school_district: Cypress Fairbanks ISD and Houston ISD (verify each address)

name: Oak Forest
summary: Mid century ranch homes, big trees, and a close knit feel just north of the Heights.
typical_homes: Mid century ranch homes and new construction
local_take: Oak Forest gives families a real yard and a quick drive to the Heights. Many buyers build new here, so lot size and flood history are the first things I check.
best_for: Young families who want a yard and a quick drive to the Heights

name: Omega Bay
summary: A small waterfront community on the bay near Hitchcock.
local_take: Omega Bay is quiet and small. Check elevation and insurance on every home.
best_for: Buyers who want quiet waterfront living

name: Palestine
summary: A historic East Texas city with the Texas State Railroad and Victorian architecture.
typical_homes: Historic homes, older homes and acreage
local_take: Palestine is far from Houston but full of character. I help clients connect with local experts there.
best_for: Buyers who want small city living and land

name: Pasadena
summary: A large, hardworking city east of Houston with affordable homes and easy access to the Ship Channel.
local_take: Pasadena gives you space and value close to the city. Inspect older homes and check nearby industry.
best_for: First time buyers and families looking for value

name: Pearland
summary: A popular family suburb south of Houston with strong schools, shopping and new communities.
local_take: Pearland is one of the best suburbs for Medical Center commuters. School district boundaries vary, so check every address.
best_for: Families who want schools, amenities and a short drive to the Medical Center
school_district: Pearland ISD and Alvin ISD (verify each address)

name: Plantersville
summary: Rolling country near the Texas Renaissance Festival grounds in Grimes County.
local_take: Plantersville is a good land option northwest of Houston. Check access and utilities.
best_for: Buyers who want land within reach of Houston
school_district: Navasota ISD and Magnolia ISD (verify each address)

name: Porter / New Caney
summary: Tall pines and new communities along Interstate 69 north of Kingwood.
typical_homes: New and newer single family homes
local_take: This area is growing fast with lots of new construction. Compare MUD taxes and flood history.
best_for: Families who want newer homes at a lower price

name: Rice / Museum District
summary: Museums, Hermann Park and Rice University set the tone for some of the most elegant streets in the city.
typical_homes: Historic homes, condos and newer townhomes
local_take: You are paying for location and neighbors like the museums and the park. Condos here can be a smart entry point into an area that rarely gets cheaper.
best_for: Buyers who want culture, green space and a central address

name: Richmond / Rosenberg
summary: Historic Fort Bend towns on the Brazos River, surrounded by growing master planned communities.
typical_homes: Older homes and new master planned communities
local_take: Richmond and Rosenberg offer lots of choices at good prices. Check flood zones near the Brazos River.
best_for: Families who want new homes and small town history

name: River Oaks
summary: Houston's most iconic address, with estate homes, the River Oaks Country Club and upscale shopping nearby.
typical_homes: Estate homes, custom new builds and high end townhomes
local_take: River Oaks is its own market with its own rules, and many homes trade quietly. Deed restrictions matter here, so review them before you plan any project.
best_for: Luxury buyers who want prestige, privacy and a central location

name: Rivercrest
summary: A small, quiet residential pocket with limited homes for sale.
local_take: Very few homes trade here each year. If you want in, set up alerts and be ready when one comes up.
best_for: Buyers who want a low key neighborhood

name: Riverside
summary: Historic Riverside Terrace, with mid century homes along Brays Bayou and a deep Third Ward history.
typical_homes: Mid century ranch homes, historic homes and new infill
local_take: Riverside offers some of the largest close in lots for the price. Check flood history carefully on streets near Brays Bayou.
best_for: Buyers who want history, bigger lots and a close in location

name: Rosharon
summary: Rural Brazoria County land south of Houston with acreage and new communities.
local_take: Rosharon is a land buyer's market. Check utilities, flood zones and road access before you buy.
best_for: Buyers who want land and space south of the city

name: Santa Fe
summary: A small town in Galveston County with acreage, horses and a close knit community.
typical_homes: Acreage homes and single family homes
local_take: Santa Fe gives you room to spread out. Check flood history and insurance costs.
best_for: Buyers who want land and a country feel near the coast

name: Sharpstown
summary: One of Houston's first master planned neighborhoods, with a golf course and incredible international food.
local_take: Sharpstown offers central access at an affordable price. The food alone makes it worth a look.
best_for: First time buyers and families looking for value

name: Shepherd Park Plaza
summary: A quiet, established neighborhood north of Loop 610 with big lots and a strong civic association.
typical_homes: 1950s and 1960s ranch homes and some new builds
local_take: Shepherd Park Plaza is a sleeper near Garden Oaks. Check flood history, since some streets sit near Little White Oak Bayou.
best_for: Families who want space and a reasonable price inside the city

name: Shoreacres
summary: A tiny bayfront city near La Porte with big lots and waterfront homes.
typical_homes: Waterfront homes and larger single family homes
local_take: Shoreacres is small and rarely has much for sale. Flood and wind insurance are the first things to price.
best_for: Buyers who want quiet bayfront living

name: Sienna
summary: A large master planned community in Missouri City with trails, parks and a water park.
local_take: Sienna has great amenities for families. Factor HOA and MUD taxes into the monthly payment.
best_for: Families who want amenities and newer homes in Fort Bend

name: South Houston
summary: A small city southeast of Houston near Hobby Airport, with affordable homes and a local feel.
local_take: South Houston is an affordable entry point close to the city. Inspect older homes carefully.
best_for: First time buyers and investors

name: Southbelt / Ellington
summary: Established southeast Houston neighborhoods near Ellington Field and the Beltway.
local_take: Southbelt offers value and easy access to Clear Lake and Hobby. School zoning varies, so check each address.
best_for: Families looking for value between Houston and Clear Lake
school_district: Pasadena ISD and Clear Creek ISD (verify each address)

name: Spring
summary: A growing north Houston suburb with Old Town Spring, trails and master planned communities.
local_take: Spring has a wide range of options and prices. School district lines vary a lot, so check each home.
best_for: Families who want newer homes and good access to Interstate 45
school_district: Spring ISD and Conroe ISD (verify each address)

name: Spring Branch
summary: Ranch houses, new builds, and some of Houston's best Korean food, all close to the Energy Corridor and Uptown.
typical_homes: 1950s ranch homes, new construction, and townhomes
local_take: Spring Branch is one of the best values close to Memorial and the Energy Corridor. New construction sits next to original ranch homes, so compare carefully street by street.
best_for: Buyers who want value, space, and a central west side location

name: Stafford
summary: A small city between Houston and Sugar Land with no city property tax and quick access to US 59.
typical_homes: 1970s to 1990s single family homes and townhomes
local_take: Stafford's tax advantage is real. Inventory is limited, so be ready to move.
best_for: Buyers who want convenience and lower taxes
school_district: Stafford MSD and Fort Bend ISD (verify each address)

name: Sugar Land
summary: Parks everywhere, planned communities, and one of the most diverse food scenes in Greater Houston.
typical_homes: Single family homes in master planned communities
local_take: Sugar Land is one of the most complete suburbs in Houston, with parks, food and strong schools in one place. Ask which levee district a home is in before you fall in love with it.
best_for: Families who want space, parks, and strong schools

name: Summerwood / Lakeshore
summary: Master planned communities near Lake Houston with parks, lakes and newer homes.
local_take: You get newer construction and amenities for a good price. Factor HOA dues and taxes into the monthly budget.
best_for: Families who want newer homes and amenities in northeast Houston

name: Surfside
summary: A small beach town near Freeport with a laid back, old Texas coast feel.
local_take: Surfside is one of the most relaxed beaches near Houston. Insurance and beach access rules come first.
best_for: Beach lovers and rental investors

name: Tanglewood
summary: Wide lots, tall pines, and a boulevard made for evening walks, right next to Uptown.
typical_homes: Custom and estate homes on large, tree lined lots
local_take: Tanglewood is one of my favorite neighborhoods in the city, with big lots right next to Uptown. Lot size and location on the street matter more than the house in many cases.
best_for: Buyers who want an established luxury neighborhood minutes from the Galleria

name: Teichman / Channelview
summary: A small, working area along the Ship Channel near Channelview.
local_take: Inventory is small here. Check flood risk and nearby industrial uses before you buy.
best_for: Buyers looking for affordability near east side jobs

name: Tennessee Colony
summary: A rural Anderson County community with farmland.
local_take: This is a rural land market. Surveys and access matter most.
best_for: Buyers who want rural land

name: Texas City
summary: A Galveston County city on the bay with affordable homes and a long industrial history.
typical_homes: 1950s to 1990s single family homes and new builds
local_take: Texas City offers good value near the coast. Check flood risk and nearby industry.
best_for: Buyers who want value and bay access

name: The Heights
summary: Porches, bungalows, and a walkable main street feel just minutes from downtown.
typical_homes: Restored bungalows, new construction, and townhomes
local_take: The Heights is the neighborhood buyers ask me about most, and the best streets move fast. Historic district rules can limit changes, so read them before you plan a remodel.
best_for: People who want character, walkability, and a short drive to everything

name: The Woodlands
summary: A master planned forest community with trails, lakes, The Woodlands Mall and the Waterway.
typical_homes: 1980s to 2000s single family homes and new builds
local_take: The Woodlands is one of the most complete communities in Texas. Compare village by village, since prices and home ages vary a lot.
best_for: Families and professionals who want amenities, trees and strong schools

name: Tiki Island
summary: A canal community just off the Galveston causeway, with boat slips behind many homes.
local_take: Tiki Island is one of the closest boating communities to Houston. Check bulkheads, elevation and insurance.
best_for: Boaters who want quick access to Galveston Bay

name: Timbergrove / Lazybrook
summary: Mid century ranch homes and big trees just northwest of the Heights, with quick access to the White Oak Bayou trail.
typical_homes: Mid century ranch homes and new construction
local_take: Timbergrove is a strong alternative when the Heights feels too tight or too pricey. Some streets near the bayou have flooded, so ask for the history on every home.
best_for: Families who want Heights access with more yard

name: Tomball
summary: A historic railroad town northwest of Houston with a charming downtown and growing neighborhoods.
typical_homes: Older homes, acreage and new master planned communities
local_take: Tomball keeps its small town feel as it grows. Check the commute and future road projects.
best_for: Families who want small town charm and newer homes

name: Treasure Island
summary: A small coastal community on the Texas coast.
local_take: This is a small market with limited inventory. Insurance and elevation are the first things to review.
best_for: Buyers who want coastal living

name: Trinity
summary: A small town near Lake Livingston and the Trinity River.
local_take: Trinity is a quiet lake market. Check flood zones near the river and the lake.
best_for: Buyers who want lake access and a quiet pace

name: Tyler County
summary: Piney woods country around Woodville and the Big Thicket.
local_take: Tyler County is a land and lifestyle market. Road access and utilities come first.
best_for: Buyers who want wooded land and privacy

name: University
summary: The area around the University of Houston and TSU, where historic Third Ward streets meet new development.
typical_homes: Older single family homes, new townhomes and rentals
local_take: This area is changing quickly, which brings both opportunity and uneven blocks. Walk the street at different times of day before you buy.
best_for: Investors, students, faculty and first time buyers looking close to Downtown

name: Upper Kirby and Greenway
summary: Central and polished, with Levy Park, great restaurants and quick drives to River Oaks and the Galleria.
typical_homes: Townhomes, condos and some single family homes
local_take: Upper Kirby is one of the most convenient addresses in the city. Townhomes dominate, so compare build quality and HOA details closely.
best_for: Professionals who want a walkable, central home base

name: Walker County
summary: Huntsville and New Waverly, home to Sam Houston State University and the Sam Houston National Forest.
typical_homes: Acreage, older homes and new builds
local_take: Walker County is a good mix of land and town. Student rentals near campus are their own market.
best_for: Buyers who want land, forest and a college town
school_district: Huntsville ISD and New Waverly ISD (verify each address)

name: Waller
summary: A small town on Highway 290 northwest of Houston with acreage and new communities.
local_take: Waller is growing as Highway 290 improves. Look into MUD taxes and road plans.
best_for: Buyers who want land or new homes beyond Cypress

name: Washington Corridor
summary: Rice Military and the Washington Avenue strip, packed with townhomes, patios and weekend energy.
typical_homes: Three story townhomes and a few older cottages
local_take: Most homes here are townhomes, and many look alike from the street. Builder reputation and flood history are what separate a good buy from a headache.
best_for: Young professionals who want to walk to restaurants and Memorial Park

name: West University / Southside
summary: West U's tree lined streets, strong schools and small town feel, right next to Rice Village.
typical_homes: Newer custom homes and some original cottages
local_take: West U holds value as well as anywhere in Houston. Lots are the real asset, so expect many older homes to be priced as land.
best_for: Families who want top rated schools and a close in location

name: West of the Brazos
summary: Rural Brazoria County land west of the Brazos River, near West Columbia and Sweeny.
local_take: This area offers land at good prices. Flood zones near the river come first.
best_for: Buyers who want land near the coast
school_district: Columbia Brazoria ISD and Sweeny ISD (verify each address)

name: Westchase
summary: A business district with parks, trails and a mix of housing between Beltway 8 and Gessner.
typical_homes: Townhomes, condos and some single family homes
local_take: Westchase gives you easy access to the Beltway and Westpark. HOA health varies widely between complexes.
best_for: Professionals who want an affordable, central west side location
school_district: Alief ISD and Houston ISD (verify each address)

name: Willis
summary: A small town north of Conroe close to Lake Conroe and the Sam Houston National Forest.
typical_homes: Older homes, acreage and new builds
local_take: Willis is a quieter entry point near Lake Conroe. Commutes into Houston are long, so plan accordingly.
best_for: Buyers who want lake access and space at a lower price

name: Willowbrook South
summary: Established neighborhoods near Willowbrook Mall and Highway 249 with easy access to shopping.
typical_homes: 1970s to 1990s single family homes and townhomes
local_take: Willowbrook is convenient for everyday errands and commutes. Check flood history near the creeks.
best_for: Buyers who want convenience and value in northwest Houston
school_district: Cypress Fairbanks ISD and Klein ISD (verify each address)

name: Winrock
summary: A compact townhome and condo pocket near Westheimer and Fountainview, close to the Galleria.
local_take: Winrock can be an affordable way into the Galleria area. Review HOA budgets and insurance costs closely.
best_for: Buyers who want a low maintenance home near Uptown

name: Afton Village
summary: An established Spring Branch subdivision distinguished by its own membership swim club and youth swim team, giving it a stronger built-in community/family-recreation identity than many comparably-aged neighboring subdivisions. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Amelia Oaks
summary: Specific architectural era and style could not be independently confirmed; the name pattern is consistent with either an older legacy plat or a small modern infill development common to this part of Spring Branch, but this is genuinely uncertain without a direct source. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Anniston
summary: A newer Lennar-built master-planned community in far west Katy, with homes starting in the $260s across 'Classic' and 'Watermill' home collections, still under active development as of 2026. Sold prices have ranged roughly $207,990-$486,740.

name: April Village
summary: April Village is a quiet, established subdivision from the 1970s built around a neighborhood pool, with mature landscaping and a settled, family friendly feel. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Arbor Green Condo
summary: Arbor Green is a condominium and townhome style community, not a single family subdivision. Built in 1978, it consists of 118 low rise, two story garden style units and is generally an entry level, affordable option in the 77092 area compared to nearby single family homes. Located in the 77092 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Ashford Forest
summary: Ashford Forest offers larger, competitively priced single family homes on a mix of one and two story floor plans, many updated over the years while keeping their original 1960s to 1970s footprints. Tree lined streets and an established feel are typical of this part of the Ashford community. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Ashford Forest
summary: Ashford Forest is a mature, wooded Memorial West subdivision bordered by Buffalo Bayou, offering a quiet, established feel with easy access to nearby recreational clubs and West Houston's shopping corridors. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Ashford Hollow
summary: Ashford Hollow offers midsize, reasonably priced single family homes built mostly between 1979 and 1982. It carries the same tree lined, low key feel found throughout the broader Ashford community. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Ashford South
summary: Ashford South offers well maintained, midsize single family homes built mostly in the 1960s through the early 1980s, with tree lined streets and manicured lawns. It has the settled, low key feel typical of the broader Ashford community. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Ashford Village
summary: Ashford Village is a picturesque, tree lined section of the Ashford community built primarily in the mid 1970s, with a mix of traditional single family homes on well kept lots. Residents describe a strong sense of neighborhood spirit, including community events and an active neighborhood watch. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Ashford West
summary: Ashford West offers modestly sized, reasonably priced single family homes built mostly around 1969 to the early 1970s, giving it some of the most affordable entry points in the broader Ashford community. It retains the same tree lined, established feel typical of this part of the Energy Corridor. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Autumn Oaks
summary: Autumn Oaks is a small, tucked away subdivision in the heart of Memorial, mixing traditional homes with contemporary rebuilds on comfortably sized lots. It offers a quieter, lower profile alternative to some of its larger neighboring subdivisions while sharing the same schools and easy commute. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Avalon at Cypress
summary: Avalon at Cypress is a newer, upscale master-planned community from Taylor Morrison spanning more than 480 acres, marking the builder's tenth Avalon-branded community in the Houston area. It offers a polished, amenity-focused lifestyle for buyers drawn to new construction on the western edge of Cypress. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Avalon at Riverstone
summary: Newer luxury section of Riverstone (built 2012-2020) with resort-style amenities and homes typically $760K-$1.6M+.

name: Barkers Landing
summary: Barkers Landing is a tight knit community of 364 homes built around an active pool and tennis club scene, with families often citing the swim team and tennis leagues as part of the neighborhood's identity. Its proximity to Terry Hershey Park and the Barker Reservoir gives it an unusually green, outdoorsy feel for its location. Located in the 77079 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Barrington Place
summary: Established Sugar Land community (built 1983-1998) off Eldridge Rd with a rentable clubhouse, homes typically $245K-$385K.

name: Bauer Crossing
summary: Public data specific to this plat is thin. Based on its zip code and general Spring Branch development patterns, it is likely a modest single-family subdivision from the postwar/mid-century Houston suburban expansion, but this has not been independently confirmed for this specific plat. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Bayou Glen
summary: Bayou Glen Road is a leafy, established street within the Tanglewood neighborhood, offering the classic Tanglewood lifestyle of mature trees, larger lots, and proximity to the bayou. It suits buyers looking for a Tanglewood address with a quieter, more residential feel. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Bergamo
summary: A brand-new 71.5-acre, 260-home community from Dallas-based developer Wilbow Corporation with Ashton Woods as first builder; homes starting from roughly $388,740 for the smallest plan. Sold prices have ranged roughly $289,990-$439,000.

name: Binglewood
summary: A legacy 1950s-60s single-family subdivision of 741 homes across six sections, organized around a strong, long-running civic association rather than commercial amenities. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Briar Lake
summary: Briar Lake is a quiet, mature subdivision that is part of a larger multi neighborhood community association, giving residents a settled, established feel with shared upkeep of common areas. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Briar Village
summary: Briar Village blends mid century ranch homes with newer Colonial, Tudor, and Mediterranean style construction under a canopy of towering oaks. Its active social calendar, from a Fourth of July parade to a holiday craft market, gives it a genuinely community oriented feel. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Briar Wood
summary: Briar Wood offers quiet, mature tree lined streets with traditional brick homes, fitting in with the settled, established feel of the surrounding Briar Forest area. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Briardale
summary: Briardale is an intimate, low-profile pocket of upscale homes in 77056, appealing to buyers who want Tanglewood-area prestige on a smaller, quieter street. Its tight-knit feel and mix of architectural styles set it apart from the area's larger, more prominent subdivisions. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Briarhills
summary: Briarhills is known for an unusually wide mix of architectural styles for one neighborhood, from contemporary patio homes to traditional brick two stories, built mostly from the late 1970s through the 1990s, home to roughly 665 houses. It has developed a reputation as a value oriented option for Energy Corridor employees, including oil and gas company staff looking to buy close to work. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Bridge Creek
summary: Bridge Creek is a well-established, family-friendly section within the larger Canyon Lakes West family of communities, giving residents their own dedicated amenity center plus shared access to a much larger network of parks and pools. It is a good fit for buyers who want an established neighborhood feel with resort-style extras close by. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Bridgeland
summary: Bridgeland is one of the largest and most amenity rich master planned communities in the greater Houston area, built around thousands of acres of lakes, parks, and trails. It offers a genuine small town feel inside a big community, with village center shopping, resort style recreation, and a wide range of home styles and price points. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Bridgeland Parkland Village
summary: Parkland Village is one of the distinct, nature-inspired villages within Bridgeland, one of the best-known master-planned communities in the Houston area. Its Prairie School-style architecture and abundance of parks and trails make it a strong fit for buyers who want resort-style amenities within a larger, highly amenitized master plan. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Brighton Place
summary: Brighton Place is a well-established Spring Branch-area neighborhood dating largely to the late 1970s, featuring single-family homes on generous lots (roughly a quarter-acre) in a mix of traditional and contemporary styles. Known for a strong sense of community, active resident involvement, and consistently low crime rates, it draws families drawn to its Spring Branch ISD schools and central west Houston location. Located in the 77055 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Broad Oaks
summary: Established in 1957, Broad Oaks is a quiet, country-like enclave of roughly 190 custom homes on generous, tree-filled lots bordering Buffalo Bayou. It sits between Tanglewood and the Memorial Villages, offering the same low-density, tree-covered feel with a bit more seclusion. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Broad Oaks Green
summary: This pocket appears to sit within, or immediately beside, the well established Broad Oaks neighborhood, an exclusive, wooded enclave just west of the 610 Loop known for large lots and mature landscaping. Buyers drawn to this address should confirm with their agent whether it is a distinct, separately platted community or simply a section within Broad Oaks itself. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Broad Oaks Place
summary: Broad Oaks Place refers to a small residential pocket in or near the Broad Oaks area just west of Tanglewood, sharing that neighborhood's quiet, tree-filled character and generous lots. Homes here would enjoy the same easy access to the Galleria, Memorial Park, and Tanglewood's amenities as the rest of the area. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Brook-Woods Estates
summary: Established in 1949 with ongoing infill over the decades, mixing midsize traditional homes with larger, newer construction, ranging from about 1,300 to nearly 4,750 square feet, on generous lots with a median around 14,400 square feet, notably larger than most nearby subdivisions. Pricing is upper mid range for the area, with recent values roughly $375,000 to $680,000. The feel is quiet and established, with a mix of home eras. Located in the 77092 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Brooke Smith
summary: One of Houston's earliest planned communities, established in 1905, with a mix of restored early-1900s bungalows and Victorian-era homes alongside newer infill construction. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Bunker Hill Village
summary: Bunker Hill Village is one of the six incorporated Memorial Villages cities, known for large wooded lots (often an acre or more), custom-built estate homes, and strict municipal zoning that has preserved its low-density, exclusively residential character since incorporating in 1954. It consistently ranks among the wealthiest communities in Texas, with home styles ranging from updated mid-century traditional to large new-construction estates. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Burkhardt Plaza
summary: Burkhardt Plaza is a small, established pocket within the City of Hilshire Village, the smallest and most understated of the six Memorial Villages. Lots run roughly a fifth to a half acre, and the housing stock is a mix of original 1960s ranch homes alongside newer custom construction as older homes are gradually replaced. It offers a quieter, lower-profile alternative to the larger, higher-priced Memorial Villages while still delivering SBISD schools and independent municipal services. Located in the 77055 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Campbell Woods
summary: An established Spring Branch single-family subdivision along Campbell Road, in a part of 77080 that has seen newer infill development built up around it in recent years. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Candlelight Estates
summary: An established 1960s neighborhood, with a median build year around 1962, of single story ranch homes featuring brick exteriors, low pitched roofs, and attached garages along cul-de-sac lined streets. Pricing runs solidly mid to upper range for the area, with a recent value range of roughly $458,000 to $886,000. The feel is peaceful, suburban, and tree lined. Located in the 77018 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Cane Island
summary: A premium, amenity-rich master-planned community (over 1,000 acres) developed starting around 2014-2016, now reported sold out as of December 2024, with homes that ranged from the high $200Ks to over $1M and an average sale price around $652K. Sold prices have ranged roughly $381,250-$1,985,509.

name: Canyon Lakes West
summary: Canyon Lakes West is one of Cypress's original large-scale, amenity-rich master-planned communities, spanning 1,800 acres with several distinct sections. It offers established, gated-feel suburban living with an unusually deep bench of parks, pools, and recreation centers. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Canyon Village at Cypress Springs
summary: Canyon Village at Cypress Springs is a settled, established neighborhood built in the mid 2000s, with mature trees, quiet streets, and easy proximity to everyday shopping. It suits buyers who want an established Cy-Fair address without the premium price tag of a newer master planned community. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Cedarwood
summary: Cedarwood is an established Spring Branch-area neighborhood of single-family homes, many dating to the early 1960s, situated on generous lots (roughly a quarter-acre and up) with mature tree canopy. The area blends original mid-century homes with renovations and newer construction, appealing to buyers seeking established character and larger lots close to central west Houston employment and retail hubs. Located in the 77055 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Chimneystone
summary: Established First Colony-area community (built 1982-1983) with a pool and tennis courts, homes typically $190K-$285K.

name: Cimarron
summary: One of Katy's older, well-established neighborhoods, built primarily 1975-1993, offering an affordable, mature-tree feel with modest-sized homes (median sale price around $290,000). Sold prices have ranged roughly $216,700-$319,000.

name: Cinco Ranch
summary: A large, long-established (built out roughly 1991-2016) master-planned community that is one of the top-selling in the country, ranging from mature 1990s-era sections to newer $1M+ estates, with homes generally from the $300Ks to over $1M. Sold prices have ranged roughly $290,000-$1,900,000.

name: Colony Bend
summary: Established First Colony-area community (built 1978-1988) with its own neighborhood park, homes typically $317K-$460K.

name: Commonwealth
summary: Established First Colony-area community (built 1987-1995) bordering Sweetwater, homes typically $450K-$870K.

name: Contemporary Heights
summary: A newer, gated infill development of roughly 109 townhome-style properties with a median build year of 2006, built as multi-story contemporary homes rather than historic bungalows. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Country Club Estates
summary: Country Club Estates is one of the original sections of Jersey Village built around the Jersey Meadow Golf Course, with homes dating from the early 1970s alongside newer custom construction and remodels on the same golf-adjacent lots. Lots here tend to run larger than the Jersey Village average, from around a quarter acre up to nearly an acre in some cases, and pricing reflects a premium for golf course frontage and location within the city. The mix of long-established homes and contemporary rebuilds gives the section a more upscale, established country club character within the broader Jersey Village community. Located in the 77040 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Jersey Village, TX.

name: Country Village
summary: Country Village is a well established neighborhood of larger single family homes built from the early 1970s into the 2000s, giving it more of a mix of eras than some strictly 1970s subdivisions nearby. Its location off South Kirkwood Road keeps it close to both everyday shopping and the Energy Corridor's office campuses. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Court At Pinewold
summary: Court At Pinewold is a small, exclusive gated community of large, competitively sized homes dating back to the early 1990s. It suits buyers who want a private, low traffic address with an established Tanglewood area pedigree. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Covered Bridge Condo
summary: Covered Bridge is a condominium community, not a single family subdivision, built in 1974. Units are garden style, some with wood burning fireplaces, and the community offers tennis courts and a clubhouse, giving buyers an affordable entry point into the 77092 area. Located in the 77092 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Covington Woods
summary: One of Sugar Land's earliest established communities (built 1973-1977), Cape Cod/Colonial-style homes typically $195K-$335K.

name: Creekside Villas of Memorial
summary: A gated community of upscale, low-maintenance single-family homes built in a compact, patio-home-style layout on small lots, popular with buyers who want new-construction quality and a lock-and-leave lifestyle inside the Memorial Villages market area. Homes typically fall in the $900,000, $1.3 million range with contemporary and traditional elevations. The "of Memorial" name reflects its marketing position within the broader Memorial/Memorial Villages area rather than a specific incorporated village. Located in the 77055 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Creekstone
summary: An established, single-family Katy ISD neighborhood of about 954 homes built by around 2000, with homes ranging 1,429-3,226 sq ft; historically priced $135,000-$255,000. Sold prices have ranged roughly $160,000-$380,000.

name: Cypress Creek Lakes
summary: Cypress Creek Lakes is a fully built out, established master planned community known for its extensive lakes, fountains, and trail system. It is a strong fit for buyers who want a mature, amenity rich neighborhood with resale inventory rather than new construction. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Cypress Oaks
summary: Cypress Oaks is an established neighborhood in the western Cypress area, zoned to Cypress Park High School, with a straightforward mix of single family homes. It offers a solid, no frills option for buyers focused on schools and location. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Cypress Oaks North
summary: Cypress Oaks North is a newer new home community built by Saratoga Homes, located just north of the established Cypress Oaks neighborhood. It appeals to buyers who want new construction in a fast growing part of Cypress with strong school access. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Cypress Springs
summary: Cypress Springs is an established, moderately priced subdivision in the 77433 area of Cypress, offering a quieter, more settled alternative to some of the area's newer, larger master-planned communities. It suits buyers looking for value in a well-located part of Cy-Fair. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: East Norhill
summary: The final and easternmost of the three original 1920s Norhill subdivisions, developed as a planned bungalow community with the same esplanade-and-park design principles as North Norhill. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Ella Lee Forest
summary: An established neighborhood near Ella Boulevard with a settled, home focused feel and a median home value around $584,600. Pricing sits in the upper mid range for the area, and the neighborhood shows strong long term homeownership. Located in the 77018 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Elyson
summary: A large (3,640-acre), amenity-heavy master-planned community developed by Newland, still actively building out, with homes ranging from the $300Ks to over $1M. Sold prices have ranged roughly $258,350-$1,112,088.

name: Enchanted Woods
summary: Per real-estate aggregator data (neighborhoods.com): single-family homes built 1963-1965, roughly 1,938-2,722 sq ft with 3-4 bedrooms and 2-3 bathrooms — a fairly consistent, single-phase mid-1960s development. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Falcon Landing
summary: A Fort Bend County, Katy ISD community built out by around 2003 (Lennar was a builder), with homes ranging roughly 1,694-3,129 sq ft; established, moderately priced Katy neighborhood. Sold prices have ranged roughly $321,000-$515,000.

name: Falcon Ranch
summary: A mature (built primarily 2001-2008), upper-mid-range Katy ISD neighborhood of well-manicured, tree-lined streets with a wide range of home sizes (typical home ~2,756 sq ft, 4 bed/3 bath; median sale price around $470,000; roughly 30% of homes have private pools). Sold prices have ranged roughly $315,000-$672,000.

name: Firethorne
summary: An established (built out mostly in the early-to-mid 2000s-2010s) master-planned community of about 1,400 acres with Texas Hill Country/Craftsman-influenced architecture, roughly half single-story homes, and an average sale price around $580K. Sold prices have ranged roughly $340,000-$958,762.

name: Firethorne West
summary: Part of the larger ~1,400-acre Firethorne master-planned community established in the early-to-mid 2000s/2008 onward; homes trend toward larger, newer 2-story construction (~3,300 sq ft typical, median year built around 2015), with recent median list price around $483,000 and a broad historical range from the $190s to $800s+. Sold prices have ranged roughly $359,995-$765,000.

name: Fleetwood
summary: Fleetwood is one of the older, more established communities in this part of west Houston, developed starting in 1973 with large, wooded lots and a mix of traditional and contemporary architecture. Mature trees and generous setbacks give it a more spacious, established feel than many newer subdivisions nearby. Located in the 77079 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Fonn Villas
summary: Fonn Villas was developed in the early 1960s on wooded, cul de sac and dead end streets, originally popular with employees of a nearby energy company. Despite the Villas name, it is a single family home community, with traditional houses featuring family rooms, fireplaces, and double garages on generous wooded lots. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Forest Pines
summary: Developed mostly in the 1960s and 1970s, with a median build year around 1971, and featuring modest ranch style homes on lots around 6,400 square feet. This is generally the most affordable price tier in the broader Oak Forest area, with typical values around $260,000 to $360,000. The feel is quiet and tree lined, with an active volunteer civic club. Located in the 77092 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Forest Retreat
summary: Forest Retreat is a modest-profile Spring Branch-area subdivision with homes ranging from 1950s original construction to newer builds from the 2000s, reflecting the broader Memorial-area pattern of gradual teardown-and-rebuild. Lots run roughly a fifth to a quarter acre, smaller than the estate lots found in the incorporated Villages, making it a comparatively accessible entry point into SBISD's top-rated schools. Located in the 77055 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Forest West
summary: A mid century neighborhood mixing traditional ranch and mid century modern styles on lots around 7,800 square feet. Pricing is more entry level to mid tier for the area, with typical values roughly in the $237,000 to $367,000 range and renovated homes running higher. The feel is quiet, tree lined, and suburban, with an active homeowners association. Located in the 77092 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Freeman Ranch
summary: An affordable, entry-level new-construction community (built roughly 2018-2025) by LGI Homes and Lennar, priced from the high $200s to mid-$300s - positioned as a first-time-buyer option on Katy's outer edge. Sold prices have ranged roughly $196,668-$300,000.

name: Frostwood
summary: Frostwood is one of Memorial West's most prestigious addresses, built out primarily with traditional ranch and mid century homes on large wooded lots. Mature pines and oaks give it a country in the city feel that has long made it one of the area's most sought after subdivisions. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Gates at Canyon Lakes West
summary: The Gates at Canyon Lakes West is a guarded, gated section within the larger Canyon Lakes West community, appealing to buyers who want extra privacy and security along with larger lots. It combines an exclusive, gated feel with full access to Canyon Lakes West's resort style amenities. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Gaywood
summary: Gaywood is a quiet, secluded neighborhood of just under 120 homes built mainly from the 1950s through the 1970s, bordered by Buffalo Bayou to the south. A private nature sanctuary within its boundaries and a dedicated constable patrol give it an unusually peaceful, protected feel for a neighborhood this close to major commercial corridors. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: George Heights
summary: New construction described in listings as 'modern traditional' style, built on and around De George Street - a small pocket of newer single-family homes rather than an original early-20th-century Heights subdivision. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Glenview
summary: Per real-estate aggregator data: single-family homes with a wide build-year span of 1952-2022 and a wide price range (~$345,000 to over $1,000,000), indicating a neighborhood with a substantial base of original 1950s homes alongside significant modern teardown-and-rebuild activity. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Gostick
summary: A small subdivision of roughly 75 single-family homes centered on Gostick Street in west 77008, with a median build year of 1930 and active teardown/rebuild turnover. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Grand Lakes
summary: An established, lake-oriented master-planned community in Katy with tree-lined streets and manicured common areas, with an average home sale price around $650K and average home size near 3,400 sq ft. Sold prices have ranged roughly $379,000-$1,065,000.

name: Grand Mason
summary: Grand Mason is a newer residential address centered on Grand Mason Drive, built out with community pool, fitness, trail, and lake amenities. It offers a fresh, amenity forward option in a fast growing corridor between Cypress and Katy. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Grange
summary: A brand-new (homes arriving 2025) master-planned community by Johnson Development spanning 1,130 acres and roughly 2,400 planned homes, with pricing from the $300s across eight builders. Sold prices have ranged roughly $369,490-$702,052.

name: Harding Heights
summary: A platted subdivision (recorded as Harding Heights / Harding Heights Ext) whose streets - Alexander, Dorothy, Lawrence, Ashland, Waverly and Rutland - sit within the broader Greater Heights fabric; housing is a mix of older bungalows and substantial 2010s-era infill and townhome construction (median build year around 2012 per recent sales data). Located in the 77007 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Heathwood
summary: Heathwood offers quiet, established streets with the mature trees and traditional brick homes common throughout the Energy Corridor's older subdivisions. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Hedwig Village
summary: A small (under one square mile), independently incorporated city founded by German settlers in the mid-1800s and formally incorporated in 1954 to preserve its residential character. Hedwig Village features spacious lots, mature pine trees, and a strong community identity, with home values generally in the multi-million-dollar range reflecting its affluent, low-density profile. As an incorporated municipality, it offers residents direct local governance and dedicated public safety services rather than a conventional homeowners' association. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Heights Enclave
summary: A small pocket of newer single-family infill construction (built around 2016) on streets including Princeton Street and East 28th Street, with homes averaging roughly 2,600+ square feet - modern in style rather than reflecting the area's older bungalow stock. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Heritage Grand
summary: A gated, age-restricted (55+) active-adult section built out roughly 2002-2010 within/adjacent to the larger Cinco Ranch master plan, comprising about 650 homes (552 single-family plus 98 duplex units); prices historically spanning roughly the high-$200Ks to high-$600Ks. Sold prices have ranged roughly $280,000-$470,000.

name: Hilshire Manor
summary: Hilshire Manor is a low-density residential subdivision in the Spring Branch/Memorial Villages area, featuring a mix of traditional, contemporary, and ranch-style homes, many built around 1990, on generously sized lots. It offers a quiet, green, family-friendly setting close to the incorporated Memorial Villages cities without carrying their municipal governance structure itself. Located in the 77055 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Holley Terrace
summary: Confirmed via Wikipedia's Spring Branch article as one of the subdivisions within Super Neighborhood #85 (Spring Branch Central), an area noted as having subdivisions that "still have deed restrictions." Per aggregator data: single-family homes built 1964-1968, roughly 1,478-2,407 sq ft, 3-4 bedrooms, 2-3 bathrooms, priced roughly $295,000-$439,000. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Holly Springs Circle
summary: Holly Springs Circle offers a small, quiet cul-de-sac setting with substantial, high value homes tucked within the greater Tanglewood area. It appeals to buyers seeking a private street with easy access to Uptown's amenities. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Homewood
summary: Homewood is a small, tree-lined enclave within the Tanglewood area's 77056 zip code, offering a quieter, low-key alternative close to Uptown's shops and restaurants. Most homes here were built in the late 1990s, giving the neighborhood a slightly newer feel than Tanglewood's historic core. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Houston Heights
summary: A large, architecturally diverse historic district with Victorian-era, Craftsman, and bungalow homes dating mostly from the 1900s–1930s, mixed with substantial teardown and new-construction infill on tree-lined streets. The neighborhood blends preserved historic housing stock with modern high-end rebuilds and has one of Houston's highest concentrations of protected historic structures. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Hudson Bend
summary: Hudson Bend is a small enclave of about three dozen single family homes, most built in the early 1990s, making it noticeably newer than many of its 1950s and 1960s neighbors. Tree lined streets and traditional to contemporary architecture give it a polished, low turnover feel that appeals to a range of buyers from young professionals to retirees. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Huisache Acres
summary: Huisache Acres is a quiet pocket of large, high-value homes built mostly from the 1990s through the 2010s, just outside Tanglewood's historic core. It offers buyers a newer-construction option within the same prestigious 77056 zip code. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Hunters Creek
summary: This part of the Memorial Villages is defined by large wooded lots, typically an acre or more, with a mix of surviving mid-century ranch homes and newer custom estates in French Country, Tudor, Mediterranean, and contemporary styles. It represents some of the most prestigious, highest-priced real estate in the Houston area, prized for privacy, mature landscaping, and top-tier SBISD schools. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Hunters Creek Village
summary: Hunters Creek Village is one of the most exclusive of the six Memorial Villages cities, historically cited as among the most expensive suburbs in Texas. Homes sit on large, heavily wooded lots and range from mid-century ranch houses to large custom estates in French Country, English Tudor, and Mediterranean styles, reflecting the city's strict low-density zoning and long-standing affluent character since its 1954 incorporation. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Hunterwood
summary: Hunterwood is a small, exclusive street of large-lot estate homes, with lots averaging around half an acre and larger. Original construction dates mostly to the 1970s, though many homes have since been replaced or extensively renovated into expansive, luxury residences in traditional and contemporary styles, placing it firmly in the Memorial Villages' upper price tier. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Indian Bayou
summary: Indian Bayou is a small, gated enclave prized for its privacy and mature tree cover, tucked near Tanglewood and the Galleria. It appeals to buyers who want a quiet, wooded retreat without giving up quick access to the city's core. Located in the 77057 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Indian Trails
summary: Indian Trails is a small residential pocket in the heart of the Tanglewood area, offering a mix of traditional and contemporary homes on landscaped lots just a short walk from the Galleria. It combines a quiet, small-scale residential feel with everyday access to Uptown Houston's shopping and dining. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Jasmine Heights
summary: A small, newer (built roughly 2019-2022) budget-friendly D.R. Horton community with mostly single-story homes, priced in the mid-$200s to high-$300s. Sold prices have ranged roughly $240,000-$364,000.

name: Johanna Place
summary: Could not independently confirm architectural style or era; the 'Place' naming convention is often used for small modern patio-home or townhome infill developments in inner Spring Branch, but this is an inference rather than a confirmed fact for this specific plat. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Katy Court
summary: A brand-new master-planned community (construction began 2024) built by Pulte and Newmark Homes, priced roughly from the high $300s to over $700,000 depending on section. Sold prices have ranged roughly $355,000-$870,326.

name: Katy Creek Ranch
summary: A fully built-out, established Katy ISD neighborhood dating to around 2015, built by Legend Homes, CastleRock, and Princeton Classic Homes; 722 homes ranging from roughly 1,331-4,187 sq ft, historically priced in the high-$100Ks to mid-$300Ks. Sold prices have ranged roughly $250,000-$889,000.

name: Katy Lakes
summary: A 385-acre master-planned community that broke ground in 2018 and is being built out to roughly 900 homesites by multiple builders (CastleRock, Gehan, HistoryMaker, Colina); entry-level to mid-range pricing, originally advertised from the upper $200s to mid-$400s. Sold prices have ranged roughly $335,000-$576,990.

name: Katy Reserve
summary: A brand-new Century Communities development (grand opening April 2026) with 548 planned single-family homes across two product lines ('Lonestar' and 'Liberty'), priced from the high $200s to $400s. Sold prices have ranged roughly $249,900-$380,000.

name: Kings Crossing
summary: A newer-build, 'move-up market' Katy ISD community (builders including Beazer Homes and Pulte Homes) with homes from roughly 1,500-3,600 sq ft; historical pricing cited from $189,000-$369,000, average home value around $358,100 in more recent data. Sold prices have ranged roughly $255,000-$475,000.

name: Kolbe Farms
summary: A modern (built roughly mid-2010s onward), gated urban-farmhouse-style infill community developed by InTown Homes, designed with input from noted architect Andres Duany - a distinct newer-build product in an otherwise mostly older Spring Branch submarket. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Lake Pointe
summary: Small lakefront enclave near New Territory with sold prices ranging widely from about $512K to $2.6M.

name: Lakefield
summary: Established First Colony-area community (built 1984-1986) with access to a lagoon-style pool complex, homes typically $270K-$340K.

name: Lakes of Jersey Village
summary: Lakes of Jersey Village is a newer-construction community relative to much of the surrounding area, established in the early 2000s with homes built roughly through 2010. It offers single-family homes at a reasonable price point built around a series of neighborhood lakes, giving it a more contemporary layout than the older Jersey Village core nearby. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Lakes of Parkway
summary: Lakes of Parkway is a gated, upscale community built in the mid to late 1990s around seven landscaped lakes. Homes tend toward larger, more custom designs than some of the surrounding older subdivisions, and the guarded entrance gives it a distinct sense of privacy. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Lakeside Forest
summary: Lakeside Forest is an established, deed restricted community built mostly in the 1970s and 1980s, known for large lots, mature trees, and a quiet, tranquil suburban atmosphere just minutes from major employment centers. Located in the 77042 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Lakeside Place
summary: Lakeside Place is a quiet, established neighborhood of traditional single family homes built mostly in the 1960s and 1970s. Mature trees and well kept lawns give it a settled, suburban character, and its location near Eldridge Parkway keeps daily errands and commutes short. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Lakeview Forest
summary: Lakeview Forest is a quiet, established neighborhood with mature landscaping, typical of the settled 1970s and 1980s subdivisions found throughout this part of the Energy Corridor. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Lancaster
summary: Lancaster is a community focused, family friendly subdivision in the Cypress Springs area with an active homeowners association, a community pool and clubhouse, and several small parks. It is a solid choice for buyers who want an engaged neighborhood association and everyday amenities close to home. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Langwood
summary: A 1950s-1960s single-story, mostly single-family subdivision (some later infill through the 2000s-2020s) with a notably high average household size and family orientation, sitting directly on the HISD/SBISD boundary. Located in the 77092 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Laverne Springs
summary: Public data specific to this plat is thin. Based on its zip code and general Spring Branch development patterns, it is likely a modest single-family subdivision from the postwar/mid-century Houston suburban expansion, but this has not been independently confirmed for this specific plat. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Lone Oak Village
summary: Lone Oak Village is an established, roughly 372-home community built primarily in the mid-2000s, offering straightforward suburban amenities in a central Cy-Fair location. It suits buyers who want a settled neighborhood with easy access to Cypress's schools, shopping, and golf. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Long Point Woods
summary: An older (median year built 1955) Spring Branch subdivision undergoing significant teardown-and-rebuild activity, now a wide mix of original 1950s ranch homes alongside multi-million-dollar custom new construction. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Lou Al Courts
summary: Lou Al Courts is a small, quiet street of large-lot homes within Hedwig Village, one of the more compact Memorial Villages cities. Lots run roughly half an acre to three-quarters of an acre, and the housing stock ranges from older homes to newer custom construction (including builds as recent as the late 2010s), reflecting an ongoing pattern of renovation and rebuilding in the area. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Mangum Manor
summary: Developed in the 1950s, with the city acquiring neighborhood parkland in 1956, and featuring traditional ranch style homes on lots roughly 7,500 to 7,600 square feet. Pricing is modest for the area, with typical values around $262,000 to $469,000. The feel is quiet and established, with an engaged civic club. Located in the 77092 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Marian Oaks
summary: An established, upscale single-family neighborhood in the 77024 zip code, closely tied to the City of Hedwig Village, with homes typically built from the late 1990s onward on lots averaging roughly a quarter-acre. Architecture blends traditional and modern styles, and recent sale prices have ranged from under $1 million to over $2 million, reflecting a mix of original homes and newer construction. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Marvida
summary: Marvida is one of Cypress's newer large master-planned communities, built around a widely praised resort-style amenity village known as the Island. It appeals to buyers who want brand-new construction, a strong lineup of builders, and amenities on par with some of the area's most established communities. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Mason Woods
summary: Mason Woods is a large, growing section of new construction spread across more than 300 acres of Cypress, built out by several respected national builders. It suits buyers who want a brand-new home with resort-style amenities while staying close to Cypress's established shopping and dining corridors. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Memorial Bend
summary: Memorial Bend is notable for its concentration of mid century modern homes built mostly in the mid to late 1950s. Tree lined streets, spacious lots, and an emphasis on architectural preservation give it a distinct, historic character within Memorial West. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Drive Acres
summary: Memorial Drive Acres is a quiet, established pocket of west Houston built mostly in the 1950s, where half acre lots and mature trees give the streets a country like calm just minutes from the city's business districts. Homes range from original mid century ranches to fully renovated and newly built residences, so the streetscape has real variety while staying low key and residential. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Drive Manor
summary: Memorial Drive Manor is an established mid-century subdivision (original homes dating to around 1950) featuring generously sized lots of roughly half an acre or more, streets like Lindenwood and Shasta Drives, and a mix of original ranch-style homes alongside newer custom rebuilds, consistent with the broader Memorial Villages trend of gradual redevelopment. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Estates
summary: A well-established, prestigious neighborhood in the 77024 zip code with peaceful, tree-lined streets and architectural styles ranging from mid-century modern to contemporary. Lots run large (a median of roughly 17,000+ square feet) and homes average well over 4,000 square feet, with a median construction year around the mid-1980s reflecting a mature, custom-built housing stock. Its tax ties to Hunters Creek Village place it firmly within the Memorial Villages footprint. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Forest
summary: Memorial Forest is a well established, tree canopied subdivision with an active civic club focused on maintaining neighborhood appearance, safety, and community spirit. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Glen
summary: Developed in the 1960s, Memorial Glen is a deed restricted community of around 166 homes set beneath a dense canopy of pine and oak trees. It has a peaceful, community centered feel, with an active property owners association and a private pool and tennis courts that give residents a built in social hub. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Green
summary: Memorial Green stands apart from most of Memorial West as a compact, gated, mixed use village blending luxury single family homes and townhomes with boutique shops and restaurants. It offers a walkable, low maintenance lifestyle geared toward professionals who want a lock and leave home base close to the city's major employment centers. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Hollow
summary: Memorial Hollow is a smaller, established residential pocket within the Memorial West area, sharing the mature tree canopy and quiet, deed restricted character common to its neighboring subdivisions. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Meadows
summary: Memorial Meadows is an established residential pocket within the Memorial West area offering a range of single family home sizes and price points, from moderately sized homes to larger, recently updated properties, all within the broader Memorial corridor's tree lined setting. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Parkway
summary: An established, mature suburban neighborhood built mainly in the 1970s and 1980s - one of the older subdivisions in the greater Katy area. Sold prices have ranged roughly $205,000-$345,000.

name: Memorial Plaza
summary: Memorial Plaza dates to the mid 1950s and mixes updated mid century ranch homes with new construction on large, tree lined lots. It is a stable, low turnover neighborhood where land value drives long term appreciation and the pace stays quietly residential despite its proximity to major commercial corridors. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Village Estates
summary: An established, upscale residential subdivision in the 77024 zip code featuring luxury single-family homes on generous lots with a mix of traditional, transitional, and contemporary architecture. Recent price data shows a median home value above $1.3 million with homes commonly in the 3,000, 4,000+ square foot range. The area reflects the broader Memorial Villages pattern of mature trees, quiet streets, and long-term ownership. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Memorial Woods
summary: Memorial Woods carries the same established, tree covered character shared by its Memorial West neighbors, with mature trees and a quiet, residential feel typical of this corridor's mid century development. Exact architectural style and lot sizes should be confirmed before publishing detailed customer facing claims. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Milroy Place
summary: A small enclave of about 110 homes with a median build year around 1920, mixing original Heights-era bungalows with newer infill construction on a tight street grid just east of Halbert Park. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Mirabella
summary: Mirabella is an established single-family community built out largely around 2015, offering a solid slate of recreation amenities in a central, well-connected Cypress location. It suits buyers who want a settled neighborhood feel without sacrificing easy access to shopping and schools. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Miramesa
summary: Miramesa is a popular, amenity-rich master-planned community closely connected to the larger Canyon Lakes West family of neighborhoods, known for its resort-style pool complex and shared golf privileges. It appeals to buyers who want an active, amenity-driven lifestyle in a well-connected part of Cypress. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Monarch Oaks
summary: One fact that could be independently confirmed: Monarch Oaks is listed in Houston's official super-neighborhood documentation as one of the named subdivisions within Super Neighborhood #86, 'Spring Branch East,' alongside Afton Village, Brykerwoods, Ridgecrest, Hillendahl Acres, Long Point Oaks, Pine Terrace, and Westview Terrace. Beyond that classification, specific architectural style/era was not independently confirmed. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Morton Creek Ranch
summary: A large (roughly 900-1,100+ home) master-planned community built 2008-2022 by Long Lake Ltd., with mid-range pricing (originally $165k-$356k, current range up to $800k+, median around $312,500). Sold prices have ranged roughly $223,200-$580,000.

name: Neuen Manor
summary: A newer, low-maintenance gated townhome/condo-style development featuring contemporary three-story townhomes and open-concept floor plans - a denser, newer-build product type relative to Spring Branch's older single-family stock. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: New Territory
summary: Large master-planned community (~3,200 acres, built 1990-2000) with 8 lakes, 4 pools, and homes generally $300K-$870K.

name: Nob Hill
summary: Per real-estate aggregator data: single-family homes built 1954-1962, roughly 1,888-2,633 sq ft, 3-4 bedrooms, 2-3 bathrooms — a fairly classic, well-established mid-century Houston ranch-home subdivision. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Norhill
summary: Part of a 1920s Hogg-family planned bungalow community on former Stude family land, marked by esplanade-lined streets and a walkable, small-lot layout. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: North Norhill
summary: Part of a 1920s planned bungalow subdivision developed on former Stude family land, distinguished by wide grassy esplanades and consistent early-20th-century bungalow architecture. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Nottingham
summary: Nottingham is a mature, tree canopied subdivision of traditional single family homes built mostly in the 1960s and 1970s. It has a settled, family oriented feel where good schools and easy access to shopping shape daily life. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Nottingham Country
summary: One of Katy's oldest master-planned communities, developed by Kickerillo in the 1970s-1980s, known for mature trees, larger lots, and traditional/colonial architecture, with homes generally $350K-$700K in good condition. Sold prices have ranged roughly $314,000-$776,000.

name: Nottingham Forest
summary: Nottingham Forest is a well established, heavily wooded subdivision known for its active civic association and community clubhouse. Homes are traditional in style, set on generous lots beneath a mature tree canopy. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Nottingham West
summary: Nottingham West is a family friendly, tree lined subdivision of single family homes dating mostly to the mid 1960s, with a suburban, settled feel typical of established Memorial West neighborhoods. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Oak Forest Manor
summary: Oak Forest Manor is a gated new construction community completed around 2021 to 2022 by Pulte Homes, built as a section within the larger, historic Oak Forest area. Homes sit on small lots with modern floor plans, hardwood floors, and quartz countertops, priced at a premium relative to older Oak Forest homes given new construction and the top rated, zoned elementary school. Located in the 77018 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Oak Landing
summary: Oak Landing is a well kept, mid 2000s to early 2010s built subdivision in the Cypress Springs school zone, offering a neighborhood pool and an HOA managed environment. It suits buyers looking for an established, move in ready Cy-Fair neighborhood. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Oakwood Gardens Condo
summary: A gated condominium complex offering one of the more affordable price points in this area, with individual units historically listing well under $100,000. The feel is multifamily and urban rather than the single family, ranch home character typical of the Oak Forest area proper. Located in the 77091 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Outpost Estates
summary: Established single-family subdivision in the northwestern part of the Spring Branch area; general era and architectural style not independently confirmed beyond its classification as part of Spring Branch's original older residential fabric. Located in the 77041 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Paddock
summary: Paddock is an established, neighborhood-scale community in Cypress centered on its own private recreation center, offering a quieter alternative to some of the area's larger master-planned developments. It is a solid choice for buyers who want a settled community with its own dedicated amenity space. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Park At Jersey Village
summary: The Park at Jersey Village is a residential community of single-family homes carrying the Jersey Village, TX address, giving it a close identification with the small, independently incorporated city that shares its name. Home styles are traditional suburban in character, and the neighborhood offers the appeal of Jersey Village's small-town governance and services alongside its own HOA-administered common areas. It fits a moderate price tier typical of the immediate Jersey Village area. Located in the 77040 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Jersey Village, TX.

name: Park/Pinemont
summary: This MLS label appears to correspond to a small, newly built infill pocket, most likely the community marketed as Park at Pinemont, offering deed restricted new construction homes of roughly 1,500 to 1,900 square feet, built around 2025 and 2026 on Rena Street. It sits in an established Oak Forest area pocket across from neighborhood ball fields, priced in the low to mid $300,000s. Located in the 77092 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Parkway Plaza
summary: Parkway Plaza is a quiet, established neighborhood with mature landscaping, fitting the settled feel of the surrounding Eldridge Parkway corridor. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Parkway Terrace
summary: Parkway Terrace is a gated community of roughly 800 homes built around 2009, with French provincial architecture, serene lakes, and mature oak trees, popular with energy sector professionals who want a secure, well maintained environment. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Parkway Villages
summary: Parkway Villages is a 224 acre, master planned collection of sections built with a more uniform, upscale look than some of its older neighbors. Two story brick homes in a modern traditional style are common, set among abundant green space and a genuinely tranquil, park like atmosphere. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Pech Landing
summary: A brand-new (built 2023-2024), small-footprint infill development of modern two-story single-family homes on compact lots (~2,957 sq ft) - a sharp contrast to Spring Branch's typical 1950s-60s housing stock. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Pheasant Creek
summary: Established Sugar Land community (built 1980-1992) with a pool and park, homes typically $157K-$335K.

name: Pine Creek at Canyon Lakes West
summary: Pine Creek at Canyon Lakes West is a defined, family-friendly section within the larger Canyon Lakes West master plan, built out around 2014. It combines its own neighborhood-scale amenities with the depth of a much larger connected community. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Pine Hollow
summary: Pine Hollow is a quiet residential lane of large custom homes just west of Tanglewood, prized for its wooded lots and easy reach of both Memorial Park and the Galleria. It offers an understated, low-profile alternative within the same prestigious 77056 zip code. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Pine Mill Ranch
summary: A newer (built primarily since 2008), family-oriented community of roughly 1,400+ two-story traditional homes averaging about 3,200 sq ft; mid-to-upper-range pricing typical of far-west Katy new construction. Sold prices have ranged roughly $285,000-$1,060,000.

name: Pine Shadows
summary: Pine Shadows is an exclusive enclave of large custom estates on wooded, pine-and-oak-shaded lots bordering Tanglewood. Many homes trace back to 1950s and 1960s ranch-style roots, though numerous multimillion-dollar rebuilds have reshaped the streetscape in recent decades. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Pine Terrace
summary: An older established neighborhood (median year built cited as 1951) with a mix of original ranch-style homes and renovated/newer construction, mature-tree suburban character. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Pinecrest
summary: Post-war (1950s–60s) ranch-style single-family homes on larger-than-typical inner-loop-adjacent lots with mature trees; an established, quiet, unpretentious Spring Branch feel that has seen gradual teardown/rebuild activity in recent years. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Pinelawn
summary: A small, modest subdivision tucked between Studewood and Shepherd Drive in the E 16th-E 18th Street block area, with a mix of original early-Heights-era homes and ongoing infill rebuilds. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Pinemont Landing
summary: Pinemont Landing is a brand new gated community of three story townhomes built around 2025, zoned to a highly rated elementary school. Homes are compact, around 1,800 to 1,900 square feet, with modern finishes and small fenced yards, priced at a premium new construction level for the 77018 area. Located in the 77018 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Pinemont Square
summary: Pinemont Square is a townhome style community built around the mid 2000s, offering a more moderate price point than newer construction in the area. Homes are two story with attached garages on small lots, appealing to buyers wanting a low maintenance option close to the Loop. Located in the 77092 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Pineridge
summary: Unlike most other entries in this group, Pineridge Street's housing stock is genuinely old for the area - the median home here was built around 1940, reflecting the historic Norhill-era bungalow and cottage stock, with some newer infill mixed in. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Piney Point
summary: Piney Point takes its name from the historic plat that also lent its name to the neighboring incorporated City of Piney Point Village, and the area shares that city's character of large, wooded lots and substantial custom homes in traditional, contemporary, and Mediterranean styles. It offers an upscale, established west Houston setting within the broader Memorial Villages market. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Piney Point Estates
summary: Piney Point Estates is an upscale enclave of sprawling, tree lined estate lots, with homes ranging from beautifully updated single family residences to multi million dollar custom builds. It is a quiet, low density pocket of the 77063 zip code, with a dedicated security patrol adding an extra layer of privacy. Located in the 77063 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Piney Point Village
