summary: One of the six independently incorporated Memorial Villages cities, Piney Point Village is defined by expansive wooded lots (often an acre or more), custom-built estate homes, and a deliberately preserved low-density, no-commercial-zoning environment dating to its 1954 incorporation. Home prices generally run from roughly $1 million to well over $6 million. This entry refers specifically to the incorporated City of Piney Point Village, distinct from a separate, more general "Piney Point" subdivision name sometimes used informally in the wider area. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Place Des Vosges
summary: Place Des Vosges brings a touch of French architectural flair to Uptown Houston, with a small collection of homes just steps from Uptown Park's restaurants and shops. It is a distinctive choice for buyers who want a walkable Uptown lifestyle in a boutique setting. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Plantation Lakes
summary: A lake-centered, relaxed suburban community (median year built around 2011, median home size ~1,855 sq ft, median value roughly $260,000), positioned as a mid-range, family-oriented neighborhood. Sold prices have ranged roughly $200,000-$315,000.

name: Post Oak Lane Court
summary: Post Oak Lane Court is a small, gated residential pocket set just off Post Oak Boulevard, giving residents an unusually short walk to Uptown's shopping and dining while still enjoying a private, low traffic street. It is a strong fit for buyers who want to be at the center of Uptown life without living in a high rise. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Prestwick Court
summary: Prestwick Court is a quiet, gated enclave of a handful of homes tucked into the heart of the Tanglewood area. It offers privacy and a country club address without the scale of a large subdivision, appealing to buyers who want an established, walkable connection to Uptown Houston. Located in the 77057 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Raintree Village
summary: An established Katy ISD subdivision built out mostly between 1983 and 2016, positioned as an affordable-to-mid-range family community (typical resale $165,000-$350,000). Sold prices have ranged roughly $168,500-$351,000.

name: Ravenna
summary: A newer (development began around 2012), guard-gated, Mediterranean-inspired luxury community with stucco exteriors, red tile roofs, and arched details - a higher-price-point, higher-density newer-build product within Spring Branch/77055. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Reflections
summary: Reflections is a quiet, established subdivision with mature trees and settled, family friendly streets typical of the Energy Corridor's 1970s and 1980s era neighborhoods. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Regents Court
summary: Small, low-profile residential street/court in inner Spring Branch; general area character is 1950s-60s ranch homes amid ongoing teardown-and-rebuild activity, though specifics for this particular court are thin. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Remington Grove
summary: Remington Grove is a quiet, established Cypress neighborhood of homes built mostly in the early 2010s, offering good value in the Cypress Springs school zone. It is a practical choice for buyers who prioritize schools and location over resort style amenities. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Reserve In Memorial
summary: Reserve in Memorial is a newer, gated enclave built by Sullivan Brothers Builders on a compact six acre site, a distinctly different product from the older 1960s and 1970s subdivisions nearby. Homes are new construction in the roughly 1,900 to 3,000 square foot range on smaller, low maintenance lots, appealing to buyers who want a Memorial area address without renovation work. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Reserve/West 26th Street
summary: A small pocket of modern townhome construction along the West 26th Street corridor in the Greater Heights area; note that public records show more than one similarly named development on this street (including plats recorded as 'Trails on West 26th Street'), so exact unit count and boundaries can vary by source. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Retreat at Oak Park
summary: Retreat at Oak Park is a newer, contemporary community of David Weekley homes with modern amenities, offering a fresh, low maintenance option in an otherwise well established part of west Houston. Located in the 77079 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Ridgecrest
summary: An older, established single-family neighborhood (multiple platted sections) in the Spring Branch East submarket, civic-club governed rather than amenity-HOA governed. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Ridgewood
summary: A small, roughly 136-home subdivision with a median build year of 1929, blending original cottages with higher-end modern rebuilds along streets including Le Green and Ralfallen. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Riedel Estates
summary: Riedel Estates is a small, established enclave dating to 1955, with spacious lots, mature trees, and a mix of mid century and modern custom homes. Without a mandatory HOA, residents enjoy more flexibility in property design while still benefiting from the area's overall stability and privacy. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: River Forest
summary: River Forest is a small, exclusive enclave of roughly 70 custom homes established in 1961, set on half acre or larger wooded lots along quiet, tree lined cul-de-sacs. Its name reflects its position near Buffalo Bayou, and it draws buyers looking for privacy and nature access without leaving west Houston. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Riverbend
summary: A quiet, close-knit enclave of about 65 large-lot homes bordering Buffalo Bayou, mixing original 1950s ranch houses with contemporary and newer construction, all on expansive lots with substantial driveways. Described by local agents as having a laid-back, walkable, dog-friendly character with strong resident ties, including multigenerational families and regular community gatherings. Home prices run well into the multi-million-dollar range given the large lots and bayou frontage. Located in the 77063 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Riverpark
summary: Established Brazos River-area community (built 1999-2002) with 160+ acres of parkland and homes typically $277K-$635K.

name: Roslyn Place
summary: A small pocket of brand new construction homes, built around 2025, on compact urban lots under 4,000 square feet, set among older Oak Forest area streets. Interiors typically feature high ceilings, quartz countertops, and modern finishes, priced in the upper $300,000s to low $400,000s, appealing to buyers who want new construction close to the Loop. Located in the 77092 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Royal Oaks
summary: An older (median year built ~1960), modest single-family subdivision of roughly 436 homes in the Spring Branch/77043 submarket - an affordable, established legacy neighborhood rather than a newer or gated community. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Rustling Oaks
summary: Rustling Oaks is an established community from the late 1950s and 1960s known for its mature oak trees and winding streets. It keeps a relaxed, welcoming pace, with a blend of original ranch style homes and newer custom construction reflecting decades of gradual updating. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Rustling Pines
summary: Rustling Pines is a deed restricted enclave of 128 homesites known for large, pine shaded lots exceeding a quarter acre. It blends renovated 1960s ranch homes with newer luxury construction, and a private constable patrol adds an extra layer of security. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Rutland Park
summary: A small subdivision (platted as 'Rutland Park Addition, Partial Replat') blending original bungalows with modern townhome-style infill; median build year is around 2013, reflecting substantial rebuild activity within an older plat footprint. Located in the 77007 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Sandalwood
summary: Sandalwood is an intimate, established community of fewer than 200 homes built around three private lakes, giving it a resort like feel unusual for an inland Houston neighborhood. Restricted entry points and a private security patrol add to a secluded, tight knit atmosphere, while homes range from mid century ranches to fully custom rebuilds. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Settlers Park
summary: Established First Colony-area community (built 1977-1983) with a card-access pool and clubhouse, homes typically $210K-$336K.

name: Seven Meadows
summary: An established, 1,050-acre master-planned community developed by Newland Communities beginning in the early 2000s, built around tree-lined streets and lakes, mostly on quarter-acre lots, with current pricing roughly $425,000-$745,000. Sold prices have ranged roughly $350,000-$1,135,000.

name: Shadow Oaks
summary: An established, tree-lined single-family subdivision with a mix of original homes and renovated/rebuilt properties, priced in the upper-middle range for the area. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Shadowbriar
summary: Shadowbriar is a garden home and patio home community built mostly from 1979 to 1988, offering a more low maintenance lifestyle than the larger single family lots common elsewhere in the Energy Corridor. It gives its name to the zoned elementary school that also serves several neighboring Ashford sections. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Shady Acres
summary: A rapidly transitioning infill neighborhood mixing surviving 1940s–1950s bungalows with dense modern townhome and patio-home development built since the late 1990s; among the most active teardown/new-construction zones in the greater Heights area. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Shadyvilla
summary: Inner Spring Branch (77055) subdivision built out mainly in the 1950s-60s with ranch-style homes on generously sized, tree-covered lots; like much of this part of Spring Branch it has seen significant recent teardown/new-construction infill. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Shepherd Forest
summary: An established, deed restricted community of more than 900 homes dating mostly to the mid 1950s, with a mix of traditional bungalow and updated contemporary styles on moderate sized lots around 7,300 square feet. Home values typically run roughly in the high $300,000s to $600,000s. The feel is friendly and active, with a strong civic club culture and tree lined streets. Located in the 77018 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Shepherd Oaks
summary: Shepherd Oaks is a gated community of modern, three story townhomes built around 2016, offering low maintenance living zoned to a Montessori magnet elementary. It sits at a mid tier price point, generally newer and pricier than the area's older single family stock but below brand new 2025 and 2026 construction nearby. Located in the 77018 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: Sherwood Oaks
summary: A 1960s mid-century-built, single-story ranch-home subdivision of roughly 342 homes on large (9,000+ sq ft) tree-lined lots, positioned as an established, moderately priced legacy Spring Branch community. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Silver Ranch
summary: A newer (built primarily since 2008), far-west Katy community of roughly 640+ mostly two-story traditional homes averaging about 2,900 sq ft, positioned as an upper-mid-range family community. Sold prices have ranged roughly $315,000-$825,000.

name: Southlake
summary: Southlake is a quiet, established neighborhood with a mix of single family homes and townhomes, part of the broader South Briar community association area. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Spring Branch Estates
summary: Established mid-20th-century single-family subdivision typical of Spring Branch's original post-war build-out; modest-to-moderate homes on standard suburban lots with an older, settled feel. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Branch Oaks
summary: 1950s-60s ranch-style tract housing on tree-lined streets, part of the officially recognized 'Spring Branch Central' Super Neighborhood; mix of original homes and newer infill construction. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Branch Valley
summary: Modest 1960s-era single-family homes typical of west/central Spring Branch's Beltway 8 corridor. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Branch Woods
summary: An established Spring Branch neighborhood with homes dating as far back as 1958 alongside newer custom-built luxury estates, featuring mature shade trees and a mix of traditional brick/siding and Mediterranean-style architecture. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Brook Village
summary: A newer-build (built out roughly mid-2010s to early 2020s) infill master-planned-style community by Meritage Homes offering multiple product lines - City Series and Luxe Series townhomes, and an Executive/patio home collection - in a formerly under-built pocket of Spring Branch. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Lea
summary: Older, modest single-family subdivision typical of Spring Branch West's mid-20th-century development, in a zip code now increasingly shaped by nearby Energy Corridor commercial growth and Beltway 8 access. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Meadows
summary: Modest, older single-family subdivision in the Spring Branch West / 77043 pocket, likely built out mid-20th-century like most of the surrounding area; not independently confirmed beyond general area context. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Oaks
summary: 1950s-60s ranch-style homes on tree-lined streets in inner Spring Branch; like much of 77055, an active teardown/new-construction market has been reshaping parts of the original housing stock. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Shadows
summary: An established 1960s-70s single-family suburban neighborhood with spacious lots and mature trees, predominantly single-story homes with a growing number of newer two-story infill builds. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Valley
summary: Spring Valley is a low-key, tree-lined residential pocket of the Memorial Villages/Spring Branch area featuring single-family homes on wooded lots, ranging from older ranch-style bungalows to renovated and newly built homes in traditional, contemporary, and Mediterranean styles. It offers a small-town, tight-knit feel within minutes of major west Houston retail and employment centers. Located in the 77055 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Spring Valley Creek
summary: Public data specific to this plat is thin. Based on its zip code and the general development pattern of this part of Spring Branch, it is most likely a modest single-family subdivision from the postwar/mid-century Houston suburban expansion (roughly 1950s-1970s) — but this has not been independently confirmed for this specific subdivision. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Spring Valley Estates
summary: Spring Valley Estates is a well-established subdivision with a median build date in the mid-1980s, generally on lots around a quarter acre, and a mix of traditional and contemporary architectural styles. It offers a comparatively accessible entry point into the Memorial Villages/Spring Branch school zone relative to the larger estate lots found in some neighboring Villages. Located in the 77055 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Spring Valley Village
summary: Originally settled in 1936 and incorporated in 1955 (renamed Spring Valley Village in 2007), this small, tight-knit city features a mix of updated mid-century homes and newer construction on tree-lined residential streets. It is known for strong municipal services, a notably low crime rate, and steady, gradual growth while retaining an urban-residential, walkable character within the larger Memorial Villages area. Located in the 77055 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Springdale
summary: An older (homes dating to 1953, with some new construction through 2026) single-family subdivision in the Spring Branch East super-neighborhood, priced from the high-$300Ks to over $1.2M depending on original vs. rebuilt housing stock. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Springwood Villas
summary: Public data specific to this plat is thin. The "Villas" name suggests a townhome/patio-home or small-lot product rather than large single-family lots, but this has not been independently confirmed; era of construction is also unconfirmed. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Steeple Chase Terrace
summary: Steeple Chase Terrace is a smaller, more compact community of townhome-style homes on notably tighter lots than typical Cy-Fair-area single-family subdivisions, with some construction as recent as the 2010s. It suits buyers looking for a lower-maintenance, entry-level price point within the Jersey Village market area rather than a large-lot family home. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Stonebridge Village
summary: Stonebridge Village is a quiet, established suburban neighborhood built around large, multi-gabled single-family homes, many with private pools and mature landscaping. Streets are entirely residential with a steady, predictable rhythm and generous curb appeal. It sits in a comfortable middle to upper-middle price tier for the area, appealing to families who want extra space without leaving the Cy-Fair school zone. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Stonehenge
summary: Stonehenge is a quiet, tree shaded subdivision with the classic brick ranch homes of 1970s and 1980s west Houston, along with a smaller gated patio home enclave for those who want a lower maintenance lifestyle in the same neighborhood. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Stude
summary: A small, low-profile pocket named for its proximity to Stude Park, mixing older bungalows (median home age dating to the late 1930s in available data) with newer infill construction near the park and White Oak Bayou. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Suffolk Chase Patio Homes
summary: Suffolk Chase Patio Homes offers a low maintenance, lock and leave lifestyle with smaller patio style homes, appealing to downsizers and buyers who want less yard upkeep in an established part of the Energy Corridor. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Sugar Creek
summary: Established Sugar Land golf-course community (built 1971-1988) centered on Sugar Creek Country Club, with homes from the $290Ks to over $1M.

name: Sugarmill
summary: Established Sugar Land community (built 1980-1992) off Eldridge Rd with pools, trails, and homes typically $260K-$580K.

name: Sunset Heights
summary: A historic, deed-restricted neighborhood of Craftsman bungalows and Victorian-era cottages developed starting in 1910, with new construction blended in. A minimum-lot-size ordinance adopted in 2007 has helped curb the townhome/lot-subdivision redevelopment seen more heavily in nearby areas. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Sunterra
summary: A newer (development began around 2021), rapidly growing master-planned community in far west Katy centered on two large lagoon/lazy-river amenity villages, with homes generally in the $200Ks-$600Ks range. Sold prices have ranged roughly $228,000-$685,000.

name: Sweetwater
summary: Gated luxury estate community (built 1984-2000) anchored by Sweetwater Country Club, homes typically $960K-$2.87M.

name: Tamarron
summary: A large (4,000+ planned homes) master-planned community spanning the Katy/Fulshear border (77441/77494), emphasizing green building practices, with prices ranging from the $180s to $700s. Sold prices have ranged roughly $244,350-$660,000.

name: Tangle Lane
summary: Tangle Lane is a quiet, tucked-away street within Tanglewood's tree-canopied core, offering the neighborhood's classic large-lot living in a smaller, more intimate setting. It carries the same prestige and mature landscaping as the rest of Tanglewood on a shorter, quieter street. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Tanglewood Circle
summary: Tanglewood Circle is a small, gated community carved out within the broader Tanglewood area, giving residents a private, low traffic address while remaining close to everything the neighborhood is known for. It is a good fit for buyers who want extra privacy alongside a well known Tanglewood location. Located in the 77057 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Tara Oaks
summary: A charming, established Memorial-area neighborhood in the 77024 zip code known for an upscale suburban feel, spacious lots, and a mix of traditional and modern home styles. The neighborhood sits within the broader Memorial Villages tax and market footprint, drawing both families and professionals. Note that a separately named apartment community also called "Tara Oaks" exists near Sherwood Lane in the 77092 area farther north, that complex is unrelated to this single-family subdivision. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Tealbrook
summary: Tealbrook refers to a small, established pocket of homes in the Cypress Springs area, zoned to Cypress Springs High School and set among mature trees and quiet streets. It offers an affordable, low key entry point into this well regarded Cy-Fair school zone. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Tealwood
summary: A tranquil, established neighborhood of roughly 170-plus traditional homes on large, wooded lots with mature pine and oak trees, quiet cul-de-sacs, and low-density development. Architecture is primarily traditional ranch-style and contemporary custom homes, with recent sale prices spanning a wide range reflecting both original and renovated properties. Part of the community lies within the incorporated City of Bunker Hill Village, while the rest sits in unincorporated Houston within the Memorial Villages market area. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Telfair
summary: Master-planned Sugar Land community (built 2006-2013) with resort-style pools, ~70 acres of lakes, and homes from the $490Ks to $1.18M+.

name: Terraces on Memorial
summary: Terraces on Memorial is a gated, lock and leave style community built in the mid 2000s, appealing to buyers who want a lower maintenance home with lake views along the Memorial Drive corridor. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Tesslynn
summary: Tesslynn is a small, established subdivision of mid century single family homes, mostly built in the mid 1950s, on lots generally in the 6,000 to 7,000 square foot range. Many homes are original one story ranch style houses, some updated, offering a more affordable entry point into the Oak Forest area compared to new construction nearby. Located in the 77018 zip code in the Oak Forest area of Houston, TX.

name: The Highlands (Sugar Land)
summary: Established Sugar Land community (built 1978-1983) with a clubhouse and pool, homes typically $260K-$355K.

name: The Parkway at Eldridge
summary: The Parkway at Eldridge is a manned gated community of luxury single family homes and townhomes in a Mediterranean style, with stucco exteriors, tile roofs, and lakefront walking trails developed by Kickerillo. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: The Towns of Grants Lake
summary: Low-maintenance townhome community on Grants Lake Blvd in Sugar Land's First Colony area, with a pool, spa, and full exterior-maintenance HOA.

name: Thornwood
summary: Thornwood is a mature Energy Corridor community from the 1960s and 1970s, laid out with winding streets, cul-de-sacs, and a heavy canopy of oak and pine trees. Two community pools and an active swim team give it a strong, family focused social calendar on top of its quiet, tree covered streets. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Tigowana Terrace
summary: Data is extremely limited; the one confirmed listing found was a large, high-end 5-bed/7-bath home (~5,773 sq ft, ~$1.8M), suggesting this may be a very small, newer luxury infill enclave rather than a large original-era tract subdivision — but this is based on a single data point and should not be treated as representative without further verification. Located in the 77080 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Tilbury Oaks
summary: Tilbury Oaks is a small, established subdivision tucked into the Tanglewood area, offering a quiet residential setting with the convenience of a central Uptown adjacent location. It suits buyers looking for a lower profile address within an in demand part of town. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Timber Oaks
summary: 1960s-era single-family tract housing typical of west/central Spring Branch, with mature tree cover consistent with the 'Timber' name. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Tompkins Reserve
summary: An upscale Tri Pointe Homes community, priced from the high $500s into the $700s, that is now fully built out and sold out. Sold prices have ranged roughly $510,000-$785,337.

name: Towne Lake
summary: Towne Lake is one of Cypress's signature master-planned communities, built around a 300-acre lake and its own lakeside town center, the Boardwalk. It is a largely built-out, established community, so buyers here are typically choosing mature landscaping and an active, amenity-rich lifestyle over brand-new construction. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Towne Lake Greene
summary: Towne Lake Greene is a section within the large, established Towne Lake master planned community, giving residents full access to the community's signature 300 acre lake and resort style amenities. It suits buyers who want a lake lifestyle with boating and waterfront recreation close to home. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Townewest
summary: Established Sugar Land starter-home community (built 1974-1983) with a pool, trails, and homes typically $160K-$340K.

name: Tynewood
summary: Tynewood is an upscale street within Piney Point Village featuring large lots (many over half an acre) and substantial homes, with a median size well over 5,000 square feet. Original homes date to the mid-1960s, though the street has seen significant redevelopment into expansive, luxury custom estates in traditional and contemporary styles, placing it among the higher-end offerings in the Memorial Villages. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Upland Park
summary: Mixed residential product in the 77043 Beltway 8 corridor; listing data points to at least a townhome/condo component (Upland Park Townhomes on Upland Dr) alongside any traditional single-family homes. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Upland Park Point
summary: Could not be independently characterized beyond its presumed close geographic relationship to Upland Park; treat as an extremely small/obscure platted section pending further verification. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Upland Square
summary: Public data specific to this plat is thin. The "Square" name suggests a townhome/patio-home product, but the era of construction and architectural style were not independently confirmed for this specific subdivision. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Urban Heights Homes
summary: A small, gated modern townhome/single-family community (builder: D & Q Associates, LLC) in the Shady Acres pocket of the Greater Heights area - contemporary construction rather than early-20th-century Heights housing stock. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Usener
summary: A very small, early-1900s-era plat (median build year around 1920) interspersed among the better-known Norhill subdivision along Usener Street, mixing historic cottages with newer infill. Located in the 77007 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Ventana Lakes
summary: A 777-home master-planned community built by D.R. Horton and Perry Homes, now in closeout phase, with mid-range pricing (homes originally $208k-$375k; current median value around $358,000). Sold prices have ranged roughly $275,000-$544,000.

name: Village of Oak Lake
summary: Established north Sugar Land community around Oak Lake (built 1990-2001), homes typically $283K-$408K.

name: Village West
summary: Village West is an established neighborhood of larger single family homes built between 1977 and 1991, offering somewhat newer construction than some of the immediately surrounding 1960s and 1970s sections. It shares the same quiet, tree lined character common throughout this part of the Energy Corridor. Located in the 77077 zip code in Energy Corridor, Houston, TX.

name: Village/Spring Branch
summary: Appears to be a small, gated, newer-construction infill community (branch/leaf-themed private street names suggest a single cohesive modern development, likely built in the 2010s–2020s) rather than an older legacy Spring Branch subdivision — replacing older housing stock with more upscale product, a common pattern in this part of inner Spring Branch. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Villarosa Tamarron
summary: A newer villa-style village (built starting mid-2020s by D.R. Horton) within the larger Tamarron master-planned community, priced from roughly the high $200s to $350s as an entry-level section of Tamarron. Sold prices have ranged roughly $270,100-$350,000.

name: Villas at Canyon Lakes West
summary: The Villas at Canyon Lakes West offers a smaller lot, lower maintenance villa style option inside the well established Canyon Lakes West community. It is a good fit for buyers who want the amenities of a larger master planned community with a more compact home and yard. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: West 21st Residences
summary: A small builder development (Aspen Grey Homes) of seven modern 3-story townhomes with open-concept, second-floor living and high ceilings - contemporary construction rather than a historic Heights-era product; the development has sold out. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: West Heights
summary: A separately platted historic subdivision (median build year 1935) south/west of the main Houston Heights core, along streets including Alexander, Lawrence, and Dorothy, with a mix of century-old cottages and newer construction. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: West Memorial
summary: An established, centrally-located Katy ISD subdivision built around 1990, positioned as an affordable, long-settled family community. Sold prices have ranged roughly $205,000-$339,000.

name: West Oaks
summary: West Oaks is a small, architecturally distinct enclave just east of Tanglewood proper, historically notable as the site of President George H.W. Bush's post-White House retirement home. Its horseshoe-shaped streets and varied home styles give it a character all its own, just steps from Tanglewood's amenities. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: West Twenty Fourth Lndg
summary: A small modern townhome-style subdivision along West 24th Street in the western Greater Heights/Shady Acres area, reflecting 2010s-era infill construction rather than the area's older bungalow stock. Located in the 77008 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Westbranch
summary: A 1970s-1990s suburban subdivision with varied architecture (brick ranch, split-level, Craftsman bungalow, Colonial Revival styles) on tree-lined streets with mature palmetto palms and magnolias; positioned as an affordable, car-dependent suburban community. Located in the 77041 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Westbridge
summary: Built in the mid 1990s, Westbridge is a traditional brick suburban neighborhood of single-family homes on modest, low-maintenance lots. Home styles lean toward classic one and two-story designs typical of Houston's mid-1990s production-home era. It offers an established, family-oriented feel with mature trees and sits comfortably in the moderate price tier for the Jersey Village market area. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Westchester
summary: Westchester is an established, tree canopied subdivision that runs along Buffalo Bayou, giving many homes a wooded, creekside feel. It has a close knit, active community culture built around its pool and tennis facility. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Westfield
summary: An established, older Katy-area subdivision (zip 77449) in the $250K-$370K price band as of recent sales data. Sold prices have ranged roughly $206,000-$429,000.

name: Westgate
summary: Westgate is an established residential community in southwestern Cy-Fair, built out mostly in the early 2010s, offering straightforward suburban living close to Cypress's main retail corridors. It is a good option for buyers prioritizing an established neighborhood over new construction. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Westheimer Lakes North
summary: A 287-acre planned community built primarily in the mid-2000s by Land Tejas, positioned as a value-oriented entry point (roughly mid-$100,000s to $300,000s originally; more recent resale listings run $350,000-$535,000). Sold prices have ranged roughly $231,500-$680,000.

name: Westview Terrace
summary: Platted in 1947 as reportedly the first subdivision in Spring Branch, originally built for returning WWII veterans; a mix of mid-century ranch homes alongside significant newer construction/teardown-rebuild activity, with mature oak and pine tree canopy. Located in the 77055 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Westway
summary: Per real-estate aggregator data: built 1977-1979, homes ranging roughly 870-1,598 sq ft with 2-3 bedrooms, including both detached single-family homes and attached units (condo/townhome/loft) — a notably later build era and more mixed housing stock than most other subdivisions in the area, which tend to be 1950s-60s single-family ranch homes. Located in the 77041 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Whispering Oaks
summary: Whispering Oaks is a mid-century neighborhood, originally developed in the 1950s, known for its tree-lined streets, mature oak canopy, and large lots. Home styles range from original mid-century ranch houses to contemporary custom builds, and the neighborhood has an unusual split jurisdiction, with roughly two-thirds of homes inside Houston city limits and the remainder inside the incorporated City of Bunker Hill Village. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Wilchester
summary: Wilchester is one of Memorial West's best known subdivisions, developed in the early 1960s and known for wooded lots, traditional two story brick homes, and a strong sense of community built around its club and top rated elementary school. It has a quiet, established, family focused atmosphere. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Wilchester West
summary: Wilchester West carries the same wooded, traditional character as its neighboring Wilchester, with mature trees and comfortable, established homes on generous lots just west of the original section. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Wildewood Forest
summary: 1960s-70s single-family homes on well-treed lots, consistent with the 'Forest' portion of the name; part of the broader west/central Spring Branch Beltway 8 corridor. Located in the 77043 zip code in Spring Branch, TX.

name: Williamsburg Parish
summary: A Katy ISD neighborhood built out by around 2005 with nearly 900 single-family homes ranging 1,173-3,085 sq ft; historically priced $179,900-$239,000 (median around $220,995 as of a Feb. 2020 snapshot). Sold prices have ranged roughly $239,000-$383,000.

name: Willow Pointe
summary: Willow Pointe is a deed-restricted, family-oriented neighborhood built mainly between the mid-1990s and early 2000s, with single-family homes at a range of sizes and a comparatively reasonable price point for the area. Active recreation and safety committees give the HOA a hands-on role in day to day community life, which residents often point to as a defining feature of the neighborhood. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Willowbridge
summary: Willowbridge is a single-family neighborhood that was largely built out in the 1990s, known locally for offering relatively large homes at a comparatively reasonable price point for the area. Lots and floor plans tend to be more generous than in some of the smaller nearby subdivisions, and the community has a settled, family-oriented feel anchored by its own clubhouse and pool. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Willowick
summary: Willowick is a small, exclusive enclave within the Memorial Villages featuring large estate homes, many exceeding 5,000 square feet, on generous, mature-treed lots in a mix of traditional and contemporary architectural styles. It represents some of the higher end of the Memorial Villages market, with a quiet, private, park-like residential feel. Located in the 77024 zip code in Memorial Villages, Houston, TX.

name: Willowlake
summary: Willowlake is a single-family neighborhood built mainly in the mid to late 1990s, offering midsize homes at a comparatively reasonable price point for the area. It has a quiet, established residential feel typical of the smaller subdivisions in this part of northwest Harris County, anchored by its own neighborhood park. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Winchester Country
summary: Winchester Country is a well-established, family-oriented subdivision of midsize single-family homes built mostly from the early 1980s into the 2000s, with some newer construction filling in over time. Lots are moderate in size and typical of northwest Harris County suburban development, and pricing generally sits in the reasonably affordable to mid-range tier for the area. The neighborhood has a settled, suburban feel built around its own pool, park, and clubhouse rather than a golf course. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Winchester Country Trails
summary: Winchester Country Trails is a well-established, family-oriented pocket of single-family homes built mostly between the early 1980s and late 2010s, sitting alongside a cluster of similarly named communities including Winchester Estates, Winchester Meadows, and Winchester Village. Home sizes and lot sizes are comparable to neighboring Winchester Country, and the area carries a strong homeownership rate and a stable, neighborhood feel built around nearby parks and everyday retail rather than a dedicated on-site amenity center. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Winchester Meadows
summary: Winchester Meadows is a small, tight-knit neighborhood of roughly 109 homes built mostly in the mid 1990s, offering traditional single-family suburban architecture on lots averaging around 7,600 square feet. Its intimate size and shared use of the neighboring Winchester Country pool give it a close community feel while maintaining its own separate governance. Home prices generally fall in the moderate range for the Jersey Village market area. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Winchester Village
summary: Winchester Village is a well-established single-family neighborhood in the Winchester Country area of northwest Harris County, with homes generally dating to the mid 1980s through the 1990s. Architecture leans toward traditional brick suburban styles on modest lots, priced comfortably within the middle range for the Jersey Village market area. It carries the settled, mature feel typical of long-developed Cy-Fair neighborhoods. Located in the 77064 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Houston, TX.

name: Winward Cove
summary: A newer Lennar-built community (marketed in several sub-'collections' such as Bristol, Coastline, Woodbridge, Cottage, and Wildflower), priced roughly $254,000-$412,000. Sold prices have ranged roughly $260,000-$449,990.

name: Woodbridge (of Fort Bend County)
summary: Established community (built 1999-2003) on the Sugar Land/Four Corners line with a pool and trails, homes typically $285K-$425K.

name: Woodlake Forest
summary: Woodlake Forest is an established, multi section subdivision of single family homes along Briar Forest Drive, offering mature trees and larger lots within reach of the Westchase employment and retail corridor. Located in the 77063 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Woodland Heights
summary: Platted in 1907 as a streetcar suburb, Woodland Heights is known for smaller, simpler Craftsman bungalows, American Foursquare, Queen Anne, and English Cottage homes — generally more modest in scale than the Victorian architecture of the adjacent, earlier-platted Houston Heights. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Woodland Terrace
summary: A small early-20th-century subdivision immediately next to Woodland Heights, with a similar bungalow-era streetscape but its own distinct plat; home sizes range from modest 1920s-1930s cottages to larger, newer builds. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Woodson Place
summary: A small subdivision near Woodland Heights and Norhill with a median build year of 1925; among the higher-value pockets in this group, with substantial new construction and remodeling. Located in the 77009 zip code in Houston Heights, TX.

name: Woodstream
summary: Established First Colony-area community (built 1983-1988), homes typically $275K-$453K.

name: Woodway Oaks
summary: Woodway Oaks is a small, private enclave at the end of a quiet lane just off Woodway Drive, offering a secluded feel within easy reach of Uptown Houston. It is well suited to buyers who want privacy without sacrificing a central location. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Wynden Crescent
summary: Wynden Crescent is a small, gated court of homes tucked into the Tanglewood area, offering privacy and security behind a limited access gate. It is a good match for buyers who want a compact, low maintenance footprint in a well established part of town. Located in the 77056 zip code in Tanglewood, Houston, TX.

name: Wyndham Village
summary: Wyndham Village is a single-family residential section carrying the Jersey Village, TX address, placing it within the identity of the small, independently incorporated city rather than the wider unincorporated Cy-Fair area. Homes are traditional suburban in style, and the neighborhood's location close to Jersey Village's city core gives it a settled, small-town feel. It fits a moderate price tier consistent with the broader Jersey Village market area. Located in the 77040 zip code in the Jersey Village area of Jersey Village, TX.

name: Yaupon Place
summary: Yaupon Place is an affordable, established neighborhood in the Cypress Springs school zone with a modest, low cost HOA. It is a good option for buyers who want strong CFISD schools without a large annual association fee. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Yaupon Ranch
summary: Yaupon Ranch is a quieter, established single-family neighborhood in the 77433 area of Cypress, offering a friendly, settled feel within easy reach of the area's larger retail and amenity hubs. It is a good fit for buyers who prioritize a close-knit neighborhood over a large master-planned amenity package. Located in the 77433 zip code in Cypress, TX.

name: Yorkshire
summary: Yorkshire is a low density enclave of about 150 custom homes tucked south of Memorial Drive, prized for its privacy and spacious, wooded lots. It manages to feel secluded while staying close to the Energy Corridor and west Houston's main shopping districts. Located in the 77079 zip code in Memorial West, Houston, TX.

name: Young Ranch
summary: A newer (still actively building out), roughly 400-acre master-planned community with 12 distinct home sections including an 'exclusive luxury' section; builders include Lennar and M/I Homes; prices span roughly $228,990-$835,000, with most inventory in the $250,000-$450,000 range. Sold prices have ranged roughly $328,000-$675,000.
